Processes of Evolution
¤Most traits are polygenic -variations in the trait result in a bell-shaped curve (From Unit 4)
¤Three types of selection occur:
¤Directional Selection
  nThe curve shifts in one direction
¤Stabilizing Selection
  nThe peak of the curve increases and tails decrease
¤Disruptive Selection
  nThe curve has twopeaks
explanation: Many biological traits are polygenic, meaning they are controlled by multiple genes, which typically produces a bell-shaped curve of phenotypic distribution in a population. Natural selection can act on these polygenic traits in three distinct ways: (1) Directional Selection, which favors phenotypes at one extreme of the distribution, shifting the entire curve in that direction; (2) Stabilizing Selection, which favors intermediate phenotypes, causing the peak of the curve to increase while the tails (extremes) decrease; and (3) Disruptive Selection, which favors both extreme phenotypes over the intermediate, splitting the distribution and forming two distinct peaks.

questions.q: Which type of natural selection shifts the entire phenotypic distribution curve in one direction?
questions.exp: Directional selection favors one extreme phenotype, causing the bell curve to shift in that direction.

questions.q: What happens to the distribution curve of a polygenic trait during stabilizing selection?
opts: The curve splits into two distinct peaks.
The curve shifts entirely to the left or right.
The peak of the curve increases (favoring intermediates) and the tails decrease (selecting against extremes).
The curve becomes completely flat, representing equal frequency of all phenotypes.
questions.exp: Stabilizing selection favors average phenotypes, which increases the height of the curve's peak and reduces the tails representing extreme phenotypes.
